cards.title: Introduction to HttpClient
cards.content:
HttpClient

Angular's HttpClient offers a simplified client HTTP API based on XMLHttpRequest. It returns RxJS Observables, making it easy to handle asynchronous requests.

To use it, provide it in your app config using provideHttpClient() (in Angular 15+ standalone apps).

cards.title: HTTP Methods & Observables
cards.content:
Making Requests

Use methods like get(), post(), put(), and delete().

import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http';

constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

getData() {
  return this.http.get('/api/data');
}

Because it returns an Observable, you must subscribe() to it for the request to actually be sent.

cards.title: Headers & Params
cards.content:
Headers and Query Parameters

You can configure requests with custom headers and parameters using HttpHeaders and HttpParams.

const headers = new HttpHeaders({ 'Authorization': 'Bearer token' });
const params = new HttpParams().set('page', '1');

this.http.get('/api/data', { headers, params });
